product: Product Experience Hub (PXHub) - add-on app for the Contentserv PIM (APIs, imports/exports, flow-based integrations, Excel tools for product data)
vendor: Product Experience Solutions (essentially a single founder/maintainer; no legal entity or location stated on the homepage)
green_flags:
- The product has been described consistently since at least March 2022 (as PXH), so it is not a recent invention. Source says: "The Product eXperience Hub is an external application , which is highly integrated into Contentserv. It automatically fully synchronizes with your Contentserv installation" https://web.archive.org/web/20220309153134/product-experience-solutions.com#:~:text=The%20Product%20eXperience%20Hub,with%20your%20Contentserv%20installation
- The product scope is concrete and technical: a configurable near-real-time JSON API, an import engine with staging, ETL flows and Excel round-trips, with 'Learn more' links to PXH documentation on Contentserv's own help site. Source says: "The only available (configurable) near-real time (JSON) API for Contentserv" https://product-experience-solutions.com/#:~:text=The%20only%20available%20%28configurable%29,%28JSON%29%20API%20for%20Contentserv
- The product is a genuine integration engine with concrete push and ETL capabilities, not vague marketing copy. Source says: "It enables to build any kind of PUSH scenarios, where all (changed) data is sent to a target system or stored in a storage." https://product-experience-solutions.com/#:~:text=It%20enables%20to%20build,stored%20in%20a%20storage.
yellow_flags:
- The site's data-protection text is a few lines inside the imprint, not a full privacy policy. There is no DPA, security page or certification for a tool that reads and writes your PIM data. Source says: "In general, when visiting the website of Product Experience Solutions, no personal data are saved." https://product-experience-solutions.com/legal#:~:text=In%20general%2C%20when%20visiting,personal%20data%20are%20saved.
- The registry shows a small GmbH, registered in 2020 with €25,000 share capital, with one managing director (the founder) and no reported financials. Continuity depends on one person. Source says: "Bürgermeister-Jakob-Str. 1 a, 85640 Putzbrunn, Germany" https://www.northdata.com/Product+Experience+Solutions+GmbH,+Putzbrunn/Amtsgericht+M%C3%BCnchen+HRB+259794#:~:text=B%C3%BCrgermeister%2DJakob%2DStr.%201%20a%2C%2085640%20Putzbrunn%2C%20Germany
- The traction claim of 60+ companies and 20 partners could not be confirmed by any independent source. Only two customers, Vaillant and Varo, are named on the site. Source says: "More than 60 companies and 20 Contentserv implementation partners are already using PXHub" https://product-experience-solutions.com/#:~:text=More%20than%2060%20companies,are%20already%20using%20PXHub
- PXHub depends entirely on Contentserv, which Centric Software (Dassault Systèmes) agreed to acquire in 2025 and is integrating into its own portfolio. The add-on's compatibility with Centric's future roadmap is not publicly assured. Source says: "is excited to announce that it has signed an agreement to acquire Contentserv" https://www.centricsoftware.com/press-releases/centric-software-acquisition-ai-powered-pxm-solution-contentserv#:~:text=is%20excited%20to%20announce,agreement%20to%20acquire%20Contentserv
- The site publishes no pricing or licence terms, so the buyer must establish who the contracting party is (the GmbH, Contentserv, or a partner) and what the licence covers. Source says: "PXHub handles all Integrations from / to Contentserv" https://product-experience-solutions.com/#:~:text=PXHub%20handles%20all%20Integrations%20from%20%2F%20to%20Contentserv
- Product subpages that were in the navigation as late as January 2025 are gone. The site now has only Home and Legal Note, which suggests minimal upkeep. Source says: "Home PXH PXH REST API PXH Excel PXH Import PXH Business Rules PXH Concept Legal Note" https://web.archive.org/web/20250119064814/product-experience-solutions.com#:~:text=Home%20PXH%20PXH%20REST,PXH%20Concept%20Legal%20Note
reasoning:
What decided it: It is a one-founder vendor with no privacy policy, DPA, security certification or verifiable customer base, selling software that gets deep access to your product data, so contracting, continuity and data handling must be settled first.

PXHub looks like a real niche product. It is an add-on for Contentserv (now Centric PXM) that adds APIs, imports, exports and Excel round-trips. It comes from a registered German GmbH whose founder and only managing director was Contentserv's Chief Architect, and the vendor's 'Learn more' links point to PXH documentation hosted on Contentserv's own help site. The verdict is yellow because this is a very small founder-led vendor offered for business use, and the product gets deep read/write access to your product master data. Its site has no privacy policy, data processing agreement (DPA), security certification or pricing, and nothing independent confirms the 'more than 60 companies' claim. Before committing, find out who you would sign with (the GmbH directly, or Contentserv/Centric or an implementation partner as reseller). Ask for a DPA, a security statement, a reference call with Vaillant or Varo, and the arrangements for continuity and escrow. Also confirm that PXHub keeps working with Centric's roadmap for the product after the 2025 acquisition.

What would change the call: Moves to green if the vendor provides a signed DPA and a written security statement, and a named customer (for example Vaillant or Varo) or Contentserv/Centric confirms PXHub use or reseller status. Moves to red if Centric announces it will no longer support third-party PXHub on Centric PXM, or if the customer and partner counts turn out to be false.
